git add internal/session/store.go internal/session/tombstone_purge_test.go DESIGN.md CHANGELOG.md && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(session): revise E -- clear only pending dispatch on refusal, keep the claim (P0)

Review finding P0 (Bugbot, PR #509 round 4), and my own ruling error:
E's original fix cleared all three mission sidecars (claim, delegation
binding, pending dispatch) on PurgeTombstoned's two refusal paths,
reasoned as safe because "sidecars are not audit state." True but
incomplete: mission.SessionBoundMissions reads ReadActiveMission as its
FIRST source of mission IDs, and the unsealed-lines probe uses that
list to find a session's mission live logs. Clearing the claim on a
refused pass destroys that lookup -- the NEXT purge pass finds no bound
missions, concludes the session is clean, and drops the roster,
stranding the very unsealed lines the refusal exists to protect.

Corrected: only ClearDispatchPending runs on the refusal paths. The
pending-dispatch store is pure coordination state, never consulted by
SessionBoundMissions by any path, and is the headline capture-on-resume
hazard -- clearing it is unconditionally safe and captures nearly all
the original ruling's practical benefit. The claim and the delegation-
binding sidecar now survive until a purge actually proceeds (deleteFiles's
full three-clear is unaffected -- a proceeding purge has already decided
the roster and its audit trail are safe to lose).

Both regression tests rewritten to assert the claim SURVIVES a refusal
while the pending dispatch does not; confirmed failing against a
reverted mutation reproducing the original all-three-sidecars behavior.
DESIGN.md gets a full amendment naming the general lesson (a state's
own classification does not settle whether clearing it is safe -- what
matters is whether something else uses it as a lookup key into
something that IS protected); CHANGELOG corrected to match.
EOF
)"
